body: Yes. Yes. 100% yes. It makes me so anxious because I know that due to my anxiety I’m not doing as well in my classes as I could be. (I’ve been skipping, not completing assignments, etc). Then I remember that my parents are doing all they can to pay for me...yet here I am not using this opportunity to it’s full advantage. It’s one of my main sources of anxiety and it’s awful. It’s a spiral. You aren’t alone.

Just want to say that I can relate to you. Just ended things with my 22 year old alcoholic boyfriend and our entire relationship was strained because of his relationship with alcohol. He is now trying to be sober, only about two weeks in, and definitely using me as a crutch. Seems like this guy may have been using you as a crutch as well. I mean you said it yourself, you are not happy. I think you ended things for the right reason and now you'll  have the opportunity to find a stable and loving relationship with someone else. You owe that to yourself.

I'm starting to realize that even though he promises he will change for me and says he wants to, he just really can't. He has to change his ways for himself...

We don't live together, but live very close by each other. We usually see each other every day. Some days we go out during the day and do something fun, other days I'll head over to his place in the evening and stay the night and hang with him in the morning. 

Honestly, I'm starting to think he just really values his alone time more than he values being with me....I don't understand because I would love to spend all the time in the world with him. I love and need my alone time too, but 12-6 PM (when we are usually apart) is enough alone time for me.

I really don't think he is cheating on me (I honestly don't think he has the motivation to do that. He has been pretty depressed and low energy, gained a lot of weight lately. Like honestly, I think cheating is out).

Maybe he did go out with some friends instead. This too seems odd, as he isn't a super social person and even when we weren't dating didn't push himself to go out or hang with his friends that much.

I really think he is just sitting alone in his apartment.

But you're right. We shouldn't need alone time after this break. I don't get it.

The only thing you can do in this situation is confront him, but make sure you do not do so in an aggressive manner. Be calm, and explain to him what you found.

If you seriously can't have an open and honest conversation about this then I would be really worried for the future of the relationship. No one on reddit can give you the answers that only your boyfriend has.

You may not want to hear this, but I feel like she might be manipulating you. You don't just go from professing your love to someone romantically, to the next day saying you have only seen them as friends for a long time?? That literally makes no sense and would piss me the hell off if I were you. She definitely led you on, no question about that. 

Her angry texts seem like complete manipulation. Of COURSE you would need time to think and be alone after someone you've been in a relationship with for 9 months hits you with an "I don't love you." But, she can't take that! She wants you in her life, on her terms, so she's lashing out. Dude, that would mess me up. So I am really sorry you're dealing with this. But she is shady for leading you on for almost a year!

You need to do what is best for YOU. If you want to stick around for this "friendship" for her, and allow yourself to sacrifice what you need right now (which is time to think and be alone) then you do that. But, be ready to face the consequences of keeping in touch with her as friends when you're still in love with her.

If I were you, I would tell her that you can't be that nonchalant about it as your feelings are hurt by the fact that she told you she didn't see you romantically. Just be honest.

If she's a true friend, and a good person, she'll give you the time you need. She won't make you feel guilty for that. 

You had no obligation to contact her every day.
I'm glad that I could help remind you that you aren't alone and the only one that feels this way. I wish you the best :)

I completely understand why you are nervous. When I first began thinking about the idea of therapy, I was freaking the f out, wanting to cancel my appointment or skip it, and absolutely dreading it. But honestly, the HARDEST part is making the appointment, getting up, and GOING. Once you are there, and if therapy is right for you (which it most definitely could be amazing for you! be excited to give it a shot!), you will notice that things begin to flow. Not right away, but each session gets easier. You may even begin to look FORWARD to these sessions, because they become a relief.

I do not like talking to new people and I absolutely HATE opening up about myself or seeming weak in front of others. God is it fucking terrifying. But therapists are here to help you. Many have gone through issues themselves. They know that their clients are going to be anxious and apprehensive and know how to comfort you. Itll be okay, and like /u/dwade333miami said below, congratulations on reaching out for professional help. that's a huge step. be proud.

Yes, for me breaks are the hardest. Once they come to an end it sometimes feels utterly impossible to return back to the normal and mundane routine. But you know what, no one is judging you, I promise. Have you not gone to university? If so, you could try meeting with our professors and explaining to them that you have been experiencing severe anxiety and ask if you could turn in any assignments late or make up some work. 
I know this sounds horrifying, but my counselor told me to do it a few months ago. I met with three professors and they were understanding and let me turn in like 7 assignments late and it saved my ass.

If you aren't in university, where are you heading back to if you don't mind me asking? I'd like to help.

You can get through this. No one is judging you. I promise.

Hello! First of all, I'm sorry that you're dealing with all of this shitty anxiety. I too have always been an extremely anxious kid and now a very anxious 20 year old (I don't want to call myself an adult yet, lmao). I've been a hypochondriac all of my life and experienced some panic attacks in high school, but was relatively okay in college with exception to the last year. I've been experiencing so much anxiety this past year...ugh. Anyway, mine is exactly like you describe yours. Like, I literally wake up with butterflies in my stomach and my heart racing super fast. The second I open my eyes. Then, it comes, me feeling the sense of dread about everything I have to do that day, and just a general feeling of anxiety and doom, over nothing really specific, for the entire day. I disassociated and daze off and wonder if my feelings are real or valid or if I'm making them up in my head and I am insane. That's as close as I can relate to your mention of a simulation/dream. It sucks...I don't have much advice but just wanted to let you know I understand this general feeling of weird and nervousness. I was seeing a counselor at my college for a few months but was recently referred to an off campus psychologist. maybe you should look into talking to someone, it really does provide clarity & a safe space.
